insights.title: Pace improved despite worsening running economy
insights.body: Avg pace improved by 29 sec/km (497 → 468), yet avg efficiency worsened (+0.57 ml/kg/km), suggesting compensatory effort — possibly higher neuromuscular demand or reduced fatigue resilience, especially given concurrent cadence increase (+9 spm) and absence of recovery data.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance increased sharply in October
insights.body: Zone 3 share jumped from 33% (Sep) to 49% (Oct), while Z1 dropped from 18% to 14% — indicating less easy running and more moderate-effort work, inconsistent with low-volume recovery weeks which should emphasize Z1/Z2 (>70%).

insights.title: Cadence–efficiency mismatch emerged
insights.body: Cadence rose +9 spm (146 → 155) alongside efficiency decline (+0.57 ml/kg/km), contradicting typical adaptation patterns — usually higher cadence improves economy if stride length and ground contact time are optimized; here, stride length (82.21 cm on 10/01) is within recent range (77.97–86.49), but vertical oscillation remains stable (~8.3–8.6 cm), suggesting inefficient force application.
